contents.name: Section 15.1, Category O
contents.reason: The source’s ambient abelian category and its general objects are the next pair’s declared subject; this page uses only the specialised Verma-module consequences it proves locally.

contents.name: Definition 15.1, the category O
contents.reason: Defining category O here would pre-empt the next page’s ownership of its finiteness, abelian, duality, and block interfaces rather than supporting the present Verma-only argument.

contents.name: Example 15.2, highest-weight and contragredient Verma modules in O
contents.reason: The contragredient-Verma construction belongs with category-O duality, and no planned linkage proof requires it as a separately stated construction.

Formal character of a Verma module in Section 15.1
Corollary 15.4, locally finite central action on objects of O
contents.reason: Its assertion concerns every category-O object and is needed for block decompositions, whereas the finite Verma argument here uses the scalar central action already available on a cyclic highest-weight module.

contents.name: Exercise 15.5, locally finite central action on Harish-Chandra modules
contents.reason: Harish-Chandra modules and their analytic group-theoretic hypotheses are outside this algebraic highest-weight pair and are not a premise of any proposed proof.

contents.name: Exercise 15.6, self-extensions of Verma modules
contents.reason: The Ext calculation is a projective-and-duality question; it is not needed to establish embeddings, linkage, or the finite composition-length bound for a single Verma module.

contents.name: Corollary 15.7, central-character decomposition of O
contents.reason: A categorical direct-sum decomposition into generalized central-character blocks is precisely the next page’s block construction, not an input to the present scalar-character comparison.

contents.name: Example 15.8, a semisimple generic central-character block
contents.reason: The example diagnoses a whole category-O block and uses an Ext calculation, so it cannot be honestly reduced to this page’s individual generic-Verma simplicity corollary.

contents.name: Proposition 15.12, stabilizers in h*/Q are reflection groups
contents.reason: This structural stabilizer theorem has no role in deciding whether one particular Verma homomorphism exists or in proving the directed strong-linkage relation.

contents.name: Remark 15.13, quasiparabolic stabilizers and the B2 example
contents.reason: Its exceptional stabilizer geometry neither supplies an embedding nor changes the page’s fixed dot-action convention, so including it would not serve a planned item.

Section 2, The category O
contents.reason: This is the future page’s named ambient category; carrying its general closure, filtration, and Grothendieck-group statements here would break the planned division of ownership.

contents.name: Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2, category O and its Noetherian abelian structure
contents.reason: The definition and its categorical closure proof belong with the promised category-O foundations, while this pair remains self-contained at the level of individual Verma modules.

contents.name: Lemma 2.3, filtration of an object of O by Verma quotients
contents.reason: A filtration theorem for arbitrary category-O objects is stronger than the finite-length argument required for one Verma module and is reserved for the next page.

contents.name: Definition 2.4 and Lemma 2.5, category-O characters and Grothendieck group
contents.reason: The source’s completed character ring for all objects and its Grothendieck-group factorisation are category-O infrastructure, not a prerequisite for the local Jantzen character identity.
